full_judgment:
2. The petitioner Nos. 1 to 3 filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Kushtia, against Mahtabuddin Biswas, the predecessor of the present respondents, praying for a declaration of title in the suit-land with a further declaration that the registered deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974, registered at the Kumarkhali Sub-Registry Office to be forged and not binding upon them. The defendant Mahtabuddin contested the suit by filing a written statement contending inter-alia that he is the owner of the property by virtue of a registered kabala Deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974 and that he is in possession since his such purchase. 

 3. The aforesaid Mahtab also filed a suit being the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 in the same Court against the plaintiffs of the aforesaid suit, praying for decree for declaration of his title in the suit land. 

 4. Both the above Title Suit No.301 of 1976 and the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 were heard' simultaneously. The learned Joint-District Judge dismissed the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and decreed the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995. As such, the petitioners preferred two appeals. Title Appeal No. 248 of 2002 was filed in respect of the decree of dismissal in the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and the Title Appeal No. 249 of 2002 were filed in respect of the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995. The learned District Judge, after hearing, decreed the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and dismissed the Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 and consequently allowed both the appeals. Being aggrieved, Mahtabuddin obtained the Rules. 

 6. Mr. Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing on behalf of the petitioners, submits that the defendant in Title Suit No. 301 of 1976 and the plaintiff in Title Suit No. 11 of 1995 claimed ownership in the suit-land by virtue of a forged Deed of Sale but in spite of raising such a plea of forgery, he was not able to produce the original deed and filed only a certified copy, as such, the Appellate Court rightly disbelieved the said forged deed but the High Court Division .erred in law in disagreeing with the findings of fact arrived at by .the Appellate Court, the last Court of facts. 

 8. It appears that Mahtabuddin Biswas, the predecessor of the respondents, claimed title in the suit-land, having an area of 1.66 acres of the lands in Plot Nos. 646, 601, 648 and 647 of Mouza Hizlakar, on the basis of a registered kabala Deed No. 6812 dated 12.10.1974, executed by one Indra Bhusan, the admitted original owner. But he was unable to produce the original deed and submitted only a certified copy of the same. This was not accepted by the Appellate Court as secondary evidence. 

 9. The High Court Division found that the defendant in Title Suit No. 301 of 1976, called for the concerned volume from the office of the District Registrar, Kushtia. Accordingly, one clerk from the said office brought the concerned volume in Court and after comparing the certified copy of the Deed No. 6812 with the concerned pages of the Volume, found the averments made in the certified copy to be identical with the statements made in the Volume. The said clerk deposed as DW.4 and proved that the concerned certified copy was issued by the .office of the concerned St& Registrar. The High Court Division found that this evidence adduced by the DW.4 was not denied on behalf of the plaintiffs in the Title Suit No. 301 of 1976. The High Court DiviSi6n also found that the plaintiff in the Title 'Suit No. 11 of 1995 proved his title as well as possession in the suit-land and made the Rules absolute.
